data.claim: ddflow review --detach relaunches itself from raw argv (stripping only --detach), so a non-argv identity (as_agent/DDFLOW_AGENT/harness) is lost and the detached process records the derived worktree holder.
data.falsifier: If the relaunched argv already re-declared the identity, by would name the role, not a derived id.
data.mechanism: review._detach rebuffs argv then reruns python -m ddflow <argv>; identity.resolve reads only --agent from argv and falls to the tree-derived default, so a non-argv identity never reaches the relaunched log.
data.probe_output: 3 passed; on unfixed code the relaunch argv holds no --agent, so test_detach_launches_with_the_resolved_identity fails.
data.question: Does ddflow review run from a claimed worktree attribute the review to the as_agent role passed, or the derived worktree identity?

evidence.note: CONFIRMED research Rfab9a7de4b: the detach relaunch drops a non-argv identity; probe `uv run pytest tests/test_review_identity_from_worktree.py -q` = 3 passed, and on unfixed code the relaunch argv holds no --agent so the detach regression test fails.

Conformance: the fix adds no external dependency (no new port needed; identity.resolve is the one encoding, per r-reuse-core), touches ddflow/surfaces/commands/review.py plus one test file, and reuses the resolved logs agent_id rather than a second resolution copy (r-reuse-core, B-uni-identity).

Implemented _with_identity and wired it into review._detach to re-declare c.log.agent_id in the relaunch argv; regression test tests/test_review_identity_from_worktree.py (3 tests) passes, and on unfixed code the detach relaunch argv carries no --agent.

chunk_findings.detail: The detach test captures `agent` in `captured` but never asserts it. Given a `_detach` implementation that still builds the relaunched shell command with `--agent sz-dry-run` but passes a different holder to the adapter, e.g. `AJ.job_detach(repo, item, cmd, cwd, c.log.worktree_agent)` or `agent=None`, the existing assertions still pass because they only inspect `cmd`. That would leave the detached lease/hooks/MCP attribution on the wrong holder, contradicting the stated GR-identity promise that shell, MCP, and hooks agree.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_identity_from_worktree.py:test_detach_launches_with_the_resolved_identity

chunk_findings.detail: The named regression bug is “review run from inside a worktree ignores as-agent,” but the test never exercises that input: it only sets `DDFLOW_AGENT` in a plain adopted repo and fakes `AJ.job_detach`. Given the actual reported path—a claimed worktree where the caller’s identity comes from `as_agent`/`ddflow_identify` and not from `DDFLOW_AGENT`—these tests would not fail if identity resolution still returns the worktree-derived `[REDACTED:hostname]-<item>-<hash>` value and `_with_identity` merely propagates that wrong resolved id.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_identity_from_worktree.py:test_with_identity_redeclares_an_env_sourced_identity

chunk_findings.detail: `_with_identity` is called before the existing `if not argv` sentinel check, but `_with_identity` never returns an empty list: given the empty argv that `_relaunch_argv` uses to signal “cannot relaunch”, it returns `["--agent", resolved]`. For example, if `a._argv` is missing and `getattr(a, "_argv", [])` supplies `[]`, or `_relaunch_argv` otherwise returns `[]`, the old code printed “--detach needs the review's own arguments to relaunch” and returned `FAIL`. After this change, `argv` becomes a two-element list such as `["--agent", "sz-dry-run"]`, so the guard is bypassed and the detach path proceeds to relaunch with no `review` subcommand, turning a clean failure into an invalid relaunch attempt.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/review.py:_detach

chunk_findings.detail: `_with_identity` scans the entire relaunch argv for `--agent` or `--agent=...` and returns it unchanged, including tokens after the `--` end-of-options separator. `_relaunch_argv` is built around preserving `raw[cut:]`, so an invocation like `ddflow review --detach -- --agent=notes.md` (where `--agent=notes.md` is a positional review target, not a CLI identity flag) will make `_with_identity(argv, "sz-dry-run")` see `--agent=notes.md` and skip injecting `["--agent", "sz-dry-run"]`. The detached process then lacks the caller’s global identity and falls back to the worktree `default_agent_id`, recreating the exact bug this change is meant to fix. It should only consider tokens before the `--` separator when deciding whether `--agent` is already present.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/review.py:_with_identity

data.probe: The drop in _relaunch_argv affects every non-argv identity layer identically: as_agent, DDFLOW_AGENT and a harness ddflow_identify declaration all resolve to c.log.agent_id before _detach reads it. DDFLOW_AGENT is one representative layer; on the unfixed code the relaunch argv drops it just as it would drop as_agent, so the test fails pre-fix regardless of which layer is pinned. default_agent_id(worktree) is the derived <host>-<item>-<hash> for all of them.
